title: Defense witness can’t explain discrepancy in Cale88 sales, cash inflow
summary: DTI Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo's testimony on Cale88 raises more suspicions about the banana chips exporter's inward remittances from China

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – A defense witness for Vice President Sara Duterte on Friday, November 20, admitted he could not explain the discrepancy between the cash inflows and declared sales revenues of Cale88 Foods Corporation, a company being linked to the Vice President.

On Day 45 of the impeachment trial, the defense presented Ceferino Rodolfo, Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) undersecretary for industry development and investment promotions, to establish the legitimacy of Cale88.

Rodolfo testified that Cale88 is registered as an export enterprise under the DTI-Board of Investments (BOI) and has complied with the agency’s registration requirements. He also identified the company as a micro, small, and medium enterprise (MSME).

In his interjection, Senator-judge Sherwin Gatchalian questioned the huge disparity between Cale88’s declared sales and its reported cash inflows, asking Rodolfo to explain the possible reasons behind the discrepancy.

“In relation to the operations of the company and the documents they submitted to us, we don’t see any reason for the inward remittances to exceed the declared sales revenue submitted to us,” Rodolfo said.

Rodolfo later admitted that it was his first time encountering such a discrepancy involving a company. He stressed, however, that he was not qualified to explain the figures, saying Cale88’s president, treasurer, operating officer, and export sales manager would be in a better position to do so.

Cale88, a banana chips production company partly owned by Duterte’s husband, Manases Carpio, came under scrutiny during the impeachment trial after Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) records showed that it received P776 million in cash inflows despite having only P125,000 in paid-up capital and declaring P208 million in sales.

Lawyer Alex Cabrera, who prepared a forensic financial report on Duterte’s bank and financial records, described Cale88’s business model as “implausible.” He likened its operations to a “revolving door,” which he said was a symptom of money laundering.
Senator-judge Panfilo “Ping” Lacson said the central issue was not Cale88’s legitimacy as a registered company but allegations that it may have been used as a front for money laundering.
“What we want to see is proof or records – waybills, shipping records,” Lacson said.

“I know you said earlier that those are with the Customs, but we are all wondering, at least, if the defense could refute the forensic financial analysis, and erase our doubts that Cale88 might have been used,” he added.
Defense counsel Michael Poa clarified that Rodolfo’s testimony was only preliminary, assuring senator-judges that the defense would present other witnesses to address the allegations.
“We understand what you are looking for. We have witnesses for that,” Poa said.

Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros said on October 6 that an investigation by her office showed that Cale88 Food Corporation received remittances from Chinese companies, including entities linked to China’s state-owned sector.

Prior to that, Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura told the impeachment court that Cale88 received P319 million from China and Hong Kong, based on covered transaction reports (CTRs) and suspicious transaction reports (STRs).
The National Security Council (NSC) responded to these disclosures last October by saying it would look into the reported inflow of Chinese funds to Cale88.

Vice President Duterte has generally been silent and uncritical about China’s harassment of Philippine vessels in the West Philippine Sea, which critics say could be linked to her family’s business ties with Chinese companies.

Im a related development, the Senate impeachment court has set a new schedule for the trial as it takes a brief break to give way for the Senate plenary deliberations on the proposed 2027 national budget.

Impeachment Court Presiding Officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero initially announced that the trial would resume on Thursday, November 26, reverting to its original schedule of 10 am to 2 pm. However, lead defense counsel Sheila Sison asked for the indulgence of the court, saying their witnesses are unavailable on November 26 and November 27.

“We would like to be candid to the court and say that our next witnesses are not available on November 26 and 27. Also given that we are only informed today that there will be hearings for next week and as you know, this is not our only commitment and we had also made commitments to our other engagements,” Sison said.

“We are not interested in a protracted, prolonged trial of this case and as this court has seen, the defense has been prudent with the time of this court, has not abused this court, and has not wasted three months time presenting witnesses that will eventually be withdrawn,” she said.
House prosecutor Terry Ridon asked for Sison’s remarks to be stricken from the records. He also called for consequences to be placed on the defense for lessening the days of presentation.
Escudero said he would take under advisement Ridon’s manifestation. He also said the impeachment proceedings will resume next month with the following schedule:
December 1 to 4: 10 am – 3 pm
December 14 to 17 (if necessary)
